 Osborn Makes Final Stop In Central Nebraska Before Election
 Central Nebraska Today 
 Trevor Bentley 
 Nov 2, 2026 | 3:27 PM 
 Dan Osborn In Kearney Monday. Photo by Trevor Bentley 
 Independent U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn made one final stop in Central Nebraska on Monday in Kearney as he wrapped up the final leg of his “Mama, I’m Coming Home” Tour.
 The tour’s name is a play on Ozzy Osbourne’s 1991 hit single and included 14 stops beginning October 29, traveling from Gothenburg to South Sioux City, Nebraska City and Omaha, among other communities.
 Monday’s stop was held at the Nebraska Firefighters Museum and Education Center, where Osborn thanked supporters and fielded questions from both the audience and members of the media.
 Osborn addressed several topics, including hemp in Nebraska, mental health, Medicare and Medicaid, and education across the state.
 The Senate race marks Osborn’s second run for political office. In 2024, he fell six percentage points short of defeating incumbent U.S. Senator Deb Fischer. This time around, the Omaha steamfitter believes the biggest difference between his first campaign and this one is the foundation his campaign has built, along with increased name recognition.
 “The plane’s built, and we know how to fly it,” Osborn said. “We’ve been running as a well-oiled machine.”
 Osborn also reflected on his campaign journey, highlighting his 93-county tour that took him to every corner of Nebraska. He said the state is filled with hidden gems that many people may not realize exist unless they take the time to travel.
 “Everywhere we go is full of good people, good hardworking people,” Osborn said.
 The remaining stops on Monday’s tour included Columbus, followed by La Vista in the evening.
 As for Election Day, Osborn’s message to voters was simple: “Rock the Vote.” He plans to hold an election-night watch party in Omaha while also hoping to spend some time with family.
 Osborn and Republican incumbent Senator Pete Ricketts are competing for Nebraska’s U.S. Senate seat, with the race set to be decided Tuesday during the General Election.
